A1.justification: Both complete 24-page PDFs describe the same SEA research. Text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–G are available for comparison, and relocated or renumbered content can be matched.

before.justification: v3 reports original benchmark evaluations, ablations, robustness tests and case studies in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains those original empirical results and adds the reward-hacking evaluation in Appendix C.3 and Table 10.

M1.justification: SEA's energy function, Langevin updates over logits, straight-through estimator, initialization, Top-k masking and response revision remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendices B and G.

E1.justification: AdvBench, TruthfulQA, GSM8K, MATH and HH-RLHF are retained, including the evaluations moved from v3 C.3 to v5 C.4. The new reward-hacking experiment does not identify its dataset or input population, preventing a reliable determination of whether it extends coverage.

E2.justification: SFT, BoN, RS, ARGS, CBS and Re-Control retain their membership in matched benchmark comparisons. New Table 10 uses the existing BoN family; its different N values are search-budget settings rather than new comparison methods.

E3.justification: Appendix C.3 adds evaluation using policy KL divergence and win rates judged by GPT-4o, Qwen-Max and DeepSeek-R1, comparing BoN budgets from 8 to 256. The previously reported benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix C.3 and Table 10 add a reward-hacking diagnostic comparing third-party judged quality and policy deviation for SEA and BoN. Existing ablations, prefilling attacks, reward-model sensitivity tests, dynamics analyses and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: The runtime ± reporting in Table 5 is unchanged. New Table 10 supplies point estimates without adding seed information, repeated-run counts, uncertainty intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Existing tables and figures retain their results. New Table 10 reports SEA win rates of 90.45%, 91.31% and 93.21% under GPT-4o, Qwen-Max and DeepSeek-R1, respectively, with KL 3.91; BoN-128 reports 74.62%, 70.96% and 75.77%, with KL 3.86. These are added comparison entries, not demonstrated changes to earlier benchmark performance.

T1.justification: The BoN probability argument, RLHF objective, optimal-policy derivation and Langevin equations are unchanged. The new KL diagnostic introduces no new mathematical definition, theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about continuous-space inference-time alignment. The headline relative improvements of 77.51% on AdvBench and 16.36% on MATH are unchanged.

C2.justification: v5 adds the interpretation that higher third-party win rates with KL close to BoN-128 indicate no more severe reward hacking. The previous robustness summary concerned reward-model quality. Existing mechanism explanations and the inference-latency limitation in Appendix E remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B's implementation, hyperparameter and hardware disclosures, Appendix G's prompts, and code/checkpoint access information are unchanged. The new analysis supplies no detailed reproduction instructions or judge prompts.

R1.justification: Sections 2 and D and the reference list retain the same research positioning and cited works. New C.3 cites the already listed reference 35 alongside an unresolved citation; no identifiable new work is added.

P1.justification: Author affiliation/contact information and the appendix outline are updated, and a short reward-hacking subsection is inserted. The overall narrative remains stable, but v5 duplicates the same robustness paragraph in Section 5.6 and introduces an unresolved citation in C.3.

P2.justification: v5 inserts Table 10 and relocates the previous Tables 10–11 as Tables 11–12. Figures 7–9 move from page 19 to page 20 without changed graphics. Subsequent table renumbering and text reflow produce limited layout changes.

improvement.justification: The added reward-hacking comparison could strengthen the empirical support through three third-party judges and KL measurements. However, Table 10 lacks an identified dataset, base model, sample count and win-rate reference or judging procedure, leaving the significance of this addition unclear. Together with the duplicated Section 5.6 paragraph and unresolved citation, these limitations prevent a reliable judgment of net quality improvement.
